title: Open Problem: Polynomial-time MWIS on even-hole-free graphs
statement_text: Does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm for the Maximum Weight Independent Set problem on even-hole-free graphs?
context_text: A hole is an induced cycle of length at least four; a graph is even-hole-free if it has no hole of even length. The tree independence number of a tree decomposition is the maximum, over its bags, of the independence number of the subgraph induced by the bag, and the tree independence number of $G$ is the minimum of this over all tree decompositions of $G$. On even-hole-free graphs Maximum Weight Clique is polynomial, whereas for Maximum Weight Independent Set (MWIS) and Coloring the existence of polynomial-time algorithms remains open, in stark contrast with perfect graphs, for which polynomial algorithms (Grötschel, Lovász and Schrijver) have been known since 1981. The authors prove that every $n$-vertex even-hole-free graph has tree independence number $O(\log^{10}n)$, and that such a decomposition can be computed in quasi-polynomial time $2^{O(\log^{20}n)}$. Consequently MWIS (and many other problems, e.g. Feedback Vertex Set and $k$-Coloring for fixed $k$) can be solved in quasi-polynomial time $2^{O(\log^c n)}$ on even-hole-free graphs, so they are not NP-hard unless every problem in NP has a quasi-polynomial algorithm; earlier, a quasi-polynomial-time $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation was known. The authors stress that polynomial algorithms would need significant new ideas: even an $O(\log n)$ bound on the tree independence number would only give quasi-polynomial time.
notes: Stated in prose in the introduction without a labelled theorem environment; the paper provides quasi-polynomial-time progress but leaves polynomial-time open.
paper_title: Tree Independence Number IV. Even-hole-free Graphs

title: Open Problem: Polynomial-time Coloring on even-hole-free graphs
statement_text: Does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm for the Coloring problem (computing the chromatic number) on even-hole-free graphs?
context_text: A hole is an induced cycle of length at least four; a graph is even-hole-free if it has no hole of even length. The tree independence number of a tree decomposition is the maximum, over its bags, of the independence number of the subgraph induced by the bag, and the tree independence number of $G$ is the minimum of this over all tree decompositions of $G$. On even-hole-free graphs Maximum Weight Clique is polynomial, whereas for Maximum Weight Independent Set (MWIS) and Coloring the existence of polynomial-time algorithms remains open, in stark contrast with perfect graphs, for which polynomial algorithms (Grötschel, Lovász and Schrijver) have been known since 1981. The authors prove that every $n$-vertex even-hole-free graph has tree independence number $O(\log^{10}n)$, and that such a decomposition can be computed in quasi-polynomial time $2^{O(\log^{20}n)}$. For every fixed $k$, $k$-Coloring is solvable on even-hole-free graphs (since $K_{k+1}$ is not $k$-colorable and $K_t$-free even-hole-free graphs have logarithmic treewidth, this even gives a polynomial algorithm for fixed $k$), but the complexity of Coloring with $k$ part of the input, i.e. computing the chromatic number, is not settled by these results and remains open.
notes: Stated in prose in the introduction without a labelled theorem environment; paired with the MWIS open problem as long-standing open questions for even-hole-free graphs.
